A.question: What is the main lesson of the passage?
options: A single comparison is always enough.
Evidence should be compared under fair conditions before making a strong claim.
Weather records are more useful than bicycle counts.
School newspapers should avoid using numbers.
A.evidence: The final article included the wider set of numbers and explained when they were collected.
A.evidenceJp: 最終記事では幅広い数値を示し、いつ集めた数字かも説明しました。
A.reason: The editor improved the claim by collecting comparable data and explaining its limits.

A.question: Why did the editor ask for four more counts?
options: To prove that buses were unnecessary.
To compare bicycle use on more ordinary days under similar conditions.
To find the rainiest day of the month.
To increase the number to 150.
A.evidence: She asked the team to count bicycles at the same time on four more ordinary school days.
A.evidenceJp: そこで同じ時刻に、通常の登校日をさらに四日選んで数えることにしました。
A.reason: The first two counts were taken under different conditions, so more comparable observations were needed.

A.question: What can be inferred from the new counts of 136 to 142?
options: Bicycle use probably rose, but the original increase looked too large.
Bicycle use certainly fell below 120.
The weather had no effect on school travel.
All students stopped using after-school buses.
A.evidence: Bicycle use probably had increased, but not as sharply as the first comparison suggested.
A.evidenceJp: 自転車利用は増えているようでしたが、最初の比較が示すほど急ではありませんでした。
A.reason: The new range supports a moderate increase rather than the dramatic 120-to-150 comparison.

A.question: Which statement is true?
options: Both original counts were made on sunny Wednesdays.
The later count was made when no after-school buses were running.
The editor removed all numbers from the article.
The four new counts were all above 150.
A.evidence: the later count came from a sunny Wednesday when no after-school buses were running
A.evidenceJp: 後の数は晴れた水曜日で、しかも放課後のバスが運行されない日でした。
A.reason: Only option B matches the stated conditions.

A.question: Choose the best completion: The editor changed the article from a simple two-number claim to a report that ___.
options: hid the collection dates
used broader evidence and stated its limits
ignored ordinary school days
claimed bicycle use had doubled
A.evidence: Readers could then see both the trend and the limits of the evidence.
A.evidenceJp: 読者は変化の傾向と、証拠の限界の両方を確認できるようになりました。
A.reason: The final report presented both the trend and limitations.

B.question: In the passage, what does 'sharply' most nearly mean?
options: suddenly and greatly
quietly
at the same time
without evidence
B.evidence: not as sharply as the first comparison suggested
B.evidenceJp: 最初の比較が示すほど急ではありませんでした。
B.reason: Here sharply describes the size/speed of the apparent increase.

B.question: Which phrase best completes the idea? The first comparison was weak because the two counts were taken ___.
options: under different conditions
by the same editor
after four extra surveys
from the final article
B.evidence: The earlier count had been taken on a rainy Monday, while the later count came from a sunny Wednesday when no after-school buses were running.
B.evidenceJp: 最初の数は雨の月曜日、後の数は晴れた水曜日でバスも運行されない日でした。
B.reason: Different weather, weekday, and bus conditions made the comparison less fair.

B.question: Why did the final article explain when the numbers were collected?
options: So readers could judge the evidence more carefully.
So readers could predict the next rainy day.
So the article would contain fewer numbers.
So the school could cancel buses.
B.evidence: Readers could then see both the trend and the limits of the evidence.
B.evidenceJp: 読者は変化の傾向と証拠の限界の両方を確認できました。
B.reason: Collection conditions help readers evaluate how strong the conclusion is.

B.question: If all four new counts had been near 150, what would most likely happen to the original claim?
options: It would gain stronger support.
It would automatically become false.
Weather records would become unnecessary in every study.
The editor would have to remove the article.
B.evidence: The new counts stayed between 136 and 142. Bicycle use probably had increased, but not as sharply as the first comparison suggested.
B.evidenceJp: 新しい結果は136台から142台で、増加は最初の比較ほど急ではないと判断されました。
B.reason: Consistently high comparable counts would strengthen evidence for a larger increase.

B.question: Which additional record would best help evaluate the bicycle-use trend?
options: Counts taken at the same time on comparable school days over several months
A list of newspaper article titles
The colors of students' bicycles
Museum opening hours
B.evidence: She asked the team to count bicycles at the same time on four more ordinary school days.
B.evidenceJp: 同じ時刻に通常の登校日をさらに四日選んで数えました。
B.reason: Repeated comparable measurements directly test the trend.

A.question: What is the main point of the passage?
options: A useful map can change its recommendation when conditions change.
The shortest route is always the best route.
Visitors should never walk after six.
Local residents should design every map.
A.evidence: The map became more useful because it described a place as conditions changed, rather than pretending one route was always best.
A.evidenceJp: 条件の変化を示したことで地図はより役立つものになりました。
A.reason: The passage emphasizes time-dependent route advice.

A.question: Why did a member return in the evening?
options: To close the museum
To photograph the route
To repair streetlights
To interview station workers
A.evidence: One member returned in the evening to photograph the route
A.evidenceJp: あるメンバーが夕方に写真を撮るため再びその道へ行きました。
A.reason: The stated purpose of returning was photography.

A.question: Which statement matches the passage?
options: The shortcut was removed completely.
The shortcut was recommended equally at all times.
The finished map recommended a well-lit road in the evening.
The group studied only the afternoon.
A.evidence: recommended a slightly longer, well-lit road in the evening
A.evidenceJp: 夕方には少し長くても明るい道を勧めました。
A.reason: Option C directly matches the final map.

A.question: Why was the shortcut uncomfortable for unfamiliar visitors later?
options: It became dark after nearby shops closed.
It became much longer at night.
The museum moved to another street.
The station closed before six.
A.evidence: the street became very dark after nearby shops closed
A.evidenceJp: 近くの店が閉まった後はとても暗くなりました。
A.reason: Darkness is the condition linked to later discomfort.

A.question: Complete the summary: The group tested the route at different times and finally ___.
options: gave different route advice for daytime and evening
deleted every shortcut
recommended the dark street at night
stopped making the map
A.evidence: The finished map showed the shortcut as a daytime route and recommended a slightly longer, well-lit road in the evening.
A.evidenceJp: 完成した地図では近道を昼間向けとし、夕方には明るい道を勧めました。
A.reason: That sentence states the final time-specific recommendation.

B.question: What does 'busiest' mean in this passage?
options: having the most people or activity
being the darkest
being the shortest
having no shops
B.evidence: asked local residents when the area was busiest
B.evidenceJp: 地元の人にも人通りの多い時間を聞きました。
B.reason: Busiest refers to the time with greatest activity/traffic.

B.question: The group did not assume one route was always best; instead it ___.
options: compared conditions at different times
used only the shortest distance
ignored streetlights
closed the shortcut
B.evidence: members compared the route at three times of day, checked streetlights
B.evidenceJp: 時間を三つに分けて道の様子を比べ、街灯を確認しました。
B.reason: They evaluated changing conditions rather than making a fixed recommendation.

B.question: Why did the group ask local residents about busy times?
options: To add information about how the area changed during the day
To learn the museum ticket price
To choose a new station
To make the shortcut narrower
B.evidence: checked streetlights, and asked local residents when the area was busiest
B.evidenceJp: 街灯を確認し、地元の人にも人通りの多い時間を聞きました。
B.reason: Resident knowledge helped assess route conditions over time.

B.question: What principle would the group most likely use for another route?
options: Check whether its safety and usefulness change with time or conditions.
Always select the narrowest road.
Never ask residents for information.
Recommend only routes near shops.
B.evidence: it described a place as conditions changed
B.evidenceJp: 条件の変化を示しました。
B.reason: The group's method centers on condition-dependent evaluation.

B.question: Which new information would be most useful for improving the evening recommendation?
options: A map of working streetlights along both routes
The museum's oldest exhibit
The station building color
The number of afternoon photographs
B.evidence: members compared the route at three times of day, checked streetlights
B.evidenceJp: 時間帯を比べ、街灯を確認しました。
B.reason: Lighting data directly relates to the evening route concern.

A.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Choosing an event by comparing real timing constraints and keeping a backup plan
Choosing the earliest event no matter what
Why city buses should run more often
Why museums should remove check-in rules
A.evidence: The planning team compared the actual time conditions rather than only the starting times.
A.evidenceJp: 計画チームは開始時刻だけでなく実際の時間条件を比べました。
A.reason: The decision was based on arrival, transport, check-in, and margin.

A.question: Why did some students worry about the 10:20 gallery tour?
options: A small train delay could make the required check-in impossible.
The gallery closed at 10:00.
Walking took only five minutes.
The workshop ended earlier.
A.evidence: one small train delay could make the required check-in impossible
A.evidenceJp: 電車が少し遅れるだけで受付時刻に間に合わない可能性がありました。
A.reason: The gallery required check-in ten minutes before 10:20.

A.question: Which statement is correct?
options: The group arrived at the museum at 9:55.
The 10:02 bus reached the museum at 10:15.
Walking took ten minutes.
The science workshop required check-in ten minutes early.
A.evidence: A city bus left the station at 10:02 and reached the museum at 10:15
A.evidenceJp: 市バスは10時02分に駅を出て10時15分に博物館へ着きました。
A.reason: Option B reproduces the timetable accurately.

A.question: Why did the 10:40 workshop provide a larger time margin?
options: Its later start and later check-in deadline allowed more time after arrival.
It was located at the station.
It had no check-in requirement at all.
The bus arrived after the workshop began.
A.evidence: the science workshop allowed check-in until five minutes before it began
A.evidenceJp: 科学ワークショップは開始5分前まで受付可能でした。
A.reason: A 10:40 start with check-in until 10:35 is more forgiving than a 10:10 gallery check-in.

A.question: The team chose the workshop because it ___.
options: reduced the risk of missing check-in without greatly lengthening the day
was the earliest activity
required no transportation
guaranteed that trains would be on time
A.evidence: The decision left a larger time margin without making the day much longer.
A.evidenceJp: 予定全体を大きく長くせず、余裕のある計画にできました。
A.reason: This is the final evaluation of the choice.

B.question: What does 'margin' mean in the final sentence?
options: extra available time
ticket price
walking distance
number of students
B.evidence: The decision left a larger time margin
B.evidenceJp: 余裕のある計画にできました。
B.reason: Margin here means spare time before a deadline.

B.question: The team kept walking as a backup ___.
options: if the bus was canceled
if the museum closed
if students disliked science
if the train arrived early
B.evidence: kept walking as a backup if the bus was canceled
B.evidenceJp: バスが運休した場合は徒歩を予備案にしました。
B.reason: The condition is stated directly.

B.question: Why was looking only at starting times insufficient?
options: Arrival, transport, and check-in deadlines also affected whether the plan would work.
Starting times were not printed.
The museum had no clock.
All activities started together.
B.evidence: The planning team compared the actual time conditions rather than only the starting times.
B.evidenceJp: 開始時刻だけでなく実際の時間条件を比べました。
B.reason: Feasibility depended on several timing constraints.

B.question: If the 10:02 bus were canceled after the group reached the station, what plan had they prepared?
options: Walk to the museum
Take the 10:36 arrival bus for the gallery
Cancel the event immediately
Move the workshop to the station
B.evidence: kept walking as a backup if the bus was canceled
B.evidenceJp: バスが運休した場合は徒歩を予備案にしました。
B.reason: Walking was explicitly retained as the backup.

B.question: Which information would be most important if the group reconsidered the plan?
options: Updated train and bus arrival times plus check-in deadlines
The color of the museum walls
Students' favorite school subjects only
The number of museum windows
B.evidence: The planning team compared the actual time conditions
B.evidenceJp: 計画チームは実際の時間条件を比べました。
B.reason: Transport and deadlines determine whether each option is feasible.

A.question: What is the main lesson of the river study?
options: A conclusion should not be broader than the measurements support.
Afternoon measurements are always wrong.
River temperature never changes in the morning.
Students should avoid revising reports.
A.evidence: A smaller claim matched the evidence better and made the report more trustworthy.
A.evidenceJp: 証拠に合った小さな主張の方が、報告を信頼できるものにしました。
A.reason: The students narrowed their claim after collecting morning data.

A.question: Why did the teacher question the claim that the river was warmer all day?
options: The students had measured only at three in the afternoon.
The students had measured only in winter.
The river had no trees.
The students used two different rivers.
A.evidence: The students realized they knew only the afternoon condition.
A.evidenceJp: 生徒たちは午後の状態しか知らないことに気づきました。
A.reason: Afternoon-only data could not support an all-day conclusion.

A.question: What happened during the second week of measurement?
options: Morning temperatures changed very little while afternoon temperatures rose on sunny days.
Both morning and afternoon temperatures fell sharply every day.
Students stopped measuring in the afternoon.
The river was measured at different places each day.
A.evidence: Afternoon temperatures still rose on sunny days, but morning temperatures changed very little.
A.evidenceJp: 晴れた日には午後の水温が上がりましたが、朝の水温はほとんど変わりませんでした。
A.reason: Option A matches the observed pattern.

A.question: What likely helped keep morning temperatures steadier?
options: Trees shaded the river in the early hours.
Direct sunlight was strongest before sunrise.
Students added cold water each morning.
The river stopped flowing in the afternoon.
A.evidence: Trees shaded the river in the early hours
A.evidenceJp: 朝早くは木が川を日陰にしました。
A.reason: The passage links early shade with the different morning condition.

A.question: After collecting more data, the students changed 'warmer all day' to ___.
options: the strongest change appeared in the afternoon
the river never became warmer
morning temperature rose the most
sunlight had no possible effect
A.evidence: they explained that the strongest change appeared in the afternoon and gave a possible reason
A.evidenceJp: 最も大きな変化は午後に見られ、その理由も説明しました。
A.reason: This is the revised, evidence-matched claim.

B.question: What does 'revised' mean in the passage?
options: changed to improve or correct
copied without checking
deleted permanently
measured with a new thermometer
B.evidence: The students revised their report. Instead of saying the river was warmer all day...
B.evidenceJp: そこで報告を修正しました。「一日中暖かくなった」とせず…
B.reason: They changed the wording to fit the evidence.

B.question: The original conclusion was too broad because the students ___.
options: knew only the afternoon condition
measured both morning and afternoon
had a full year of data
studied several rivers
B.evidence: The students realized they knew only the afternoon condition.
B.evidenceJp: 午後の状態しか知らないことに気づきました。
B.reason: Their data did not cover the whole day.

B.question: Why did the students measure at both seven and three during the next week?
options: To test whether the warming pattern also appeared in the morning
To avoid measuring on sunny days
To compare two different towns
To prove that trees caused every temperature change
B.evidence: For the next week, they measured at seven in the morning and three in the afternoon at the same place.
B.evidenceJp: 次の一週間、同じ場所で朝7時と午後3時に測定しました。
B.reason: Adding morning measurements directly tested the all-day claim.

B.question: Which statement best describes the teacher's role?
options: The teacher encouraged students to check whether their evidence justified their conclusion.
The teacher supplied the final conclusion without data.
The teacher told students to ignore morning temperatures.
The teacher moved the study to another river.
B.evidence: Their science teacher asked whether the measurements supported that conclusion.
B.evidenceJp: 理科の先生は、その測定結果だけでその結論を言えるか尋ねました。
B.reason: The question prompted evidence-based reconsideration.

B.question: Which extra data would best test whether the afternoon pattern continues beyond the studied weeks?
options: Morning and afternoon temperatures collected at the same place over additional weeks
Students' favorite river activities
A list of nearby town names
The number of pages in the report
B.evidence: they measured at seven in the morning and three in the afternoon at the same place
B.evidenceJp: 同じ場所で朝7時と午後3時に測定しました。
B.reason: More comparable time-series measurements would test persistence of the pattern.
